content:
A 16-year-old child indecency case ended not with a verdict, but with a death in Webb County custody and a judge's signature.

Victor Hugo Barajas-Padilla, accused in a 2010 indecency-with-a-child case, died while held in the Webb County Jail — and Associate Judge Jose Maldonado signed the dismissal order on Sept. 11, after learning of the death at a Sept. 1 status hearing, the Laredo Morning Times reported Oct. 19.

The road to that dismissal was long. Barajas-Padilla was indicted in October 2015, then failed to appear for a final pretrial hearing on April 19, 2016, and fled to Mexico, according to the Times. He remained a fugitive for nearly a decade — until March 5, 2026, when he was arrested at a Laredo port of entry through a joint effort with the U.S. Marshals Service. Six months after his capture, he was dead, and the case against him was over.

What the report does not say

No cause of death. The Times report says Barajas-Padilla died in jail custody but gives no cause, no date of death, and no word on whether an autopsy was performed or whether any review of his medical care was conducted.

No timeline of his final months. Six months passed between his March capture and the September hearing where his death was disclosed. What medical care did he receive? Was he screened on intake? The public record, as reported, answers none of this.

No statement from the jail. No comment from the sheriff's office appears in the report about the death or about custody procedures in the case.

What Webb Watch is asking

A man held in county custody died, and the public learned of it only because a judge signed a dismissal. When did Barajas-Padilla die, and of what? Was there an autopsy? Was the death reported to the Texas Commission on Jail Standards, as required? A dismissed case does not dismiss the questions. We will be asking them.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times (Malena Charur), Oct. 19, 2026; Webb Watch 956 reporting.

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: A fugitive captured in March after a decade on the run died in Webb County Jail custody — ending a 16-year indecency case with no stated cause of death.
title: The Fugitive, the Jail, and the Dismissal: 16-Year Indecency Case Ends With a Death in Custody
